newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius rupee weakens on dollar and pound. [CORRECTED 13:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Mauritius rupee weakens on dollar and pound. [CORRECTED 13:40 GMT]

text.p: The Mauritian rupee was fixed weaker against both the dollar and the pound on Friday, commercial banks' forex dealers said.
The rupee was quoted at a mean rate of 20.6425 to the dollar from 20.6015 on Thursday. Against the pound, the rupee was fixed at a mean of 32.2395 from 32.1600 on Thursday.
Money dealers said the rupee fall resulted from the dollar's strength in international markets and an acute shortage of foreign exchange at commercial banks.
The shortage put downward pressure on the rupee and was the result of export receipts failing to keep pace with demand from bank customers.

"Although the dollar is appreciating on the international front and is adding pressure on the rupee, the central bank has not intervened for quite long in the interbank forex market to bring some support," one dealer said.
The central bank last sold dollars in the interbank forex market on September 24. (Corrects date from "September 16")

The dealer added that the Mauritius Sugar Syndicate sold pounds to banks on Wednesday and Thursday. With effect from the 1996 harvest season, the Syndicate is putting on tender sale directly to the banking sector 25 percent of the sterling proceeds from sugar exports.
The central bank keeps the remaining 75 percent for market intervention.
Sugar exports are Mauritius' largest hard currency earner in net value added terms, ahead of textile exports and tourism.
